coverage_hole_geographic_assessment.hole_location_description: 12 of 50 USID_00 dominant pixels have no backup USID. Spatial analysis of RSRP images and dominance maps suggests these are concentrated at the southern peripheral lobe (~33.027-33.029N) where USID_00's dominant area becomes disconnected from the main cluster, and potentially at corners of the main cluster where USID_26, USID_41, USID_30, USID_28, and USID_31 coverage all taper simultaneously.
coverage_hole_geographic_assessment.land_use_in_hole_area: Predominantly residential, based on the real map showing continuous suburban street grid at these coordinates. No major commercial or infrastructure features identifiable specifically in the hole zone.

load_geographic_context.primary_backup_area_character: USID_26 dominant area lies W-NW of USID_00, in a similarly dense suburban residential zone adjacent to the major N-S arterial. Its coverage extends into the central-western portion of USID_00's area with good signal quality (p50=-72.27 dBm).
load_geographic_context.notes: No critical infrastructure (hospital, transit hub, emergency services) was identifiable within USID_00's small 50-pixel dominant zone from the real map. The area is uniformly residential suburban, which carries high user relevance but not critical-infrastructure classification. The 24% hole fraction is the dominant geographic risk: users in the isolated southern lobe will lose all cellular service, in a residential area with no identified alternative access.

key_findings_for_stage4: The 24% coverage hole fraction (12 pixels) is geographically concentrated in the southern isolated lobe of USID_00's dominant area (~33.027-33.029N), a residential zone where USID_26, USID_41, USID_30, USID_28 and USID_31 coverage all tapers out — these users will lose service entirely during the shutdown

The central residential core (majority of 50 dominant pixels) is interference-limited (mean SINR 5.46 dB, 60% < 5 dB) and will hand over smoothly to USID_26 (W) and USID_41 (N) with good RSRP and low load risk

No critical infrastructure (hospital, emergency services, transit hub) is identifiable within USID_00's compact dominant footprint — impact classification is high user relevance but not critical-infrastructure severity

A major N-S road corridor at the western boundary (-96.71 to -96.70W) will be affected at the USID_00/USID_26 handoff boundary; mobile users in transit may experience brief service interruption during handover

reasons: Real map was available and used for geographic correlation, reducing uncertainty significantly
Exact pixel-level location of the 12 coverage holes cannot be derived with full certainty from the images alone — southern lobe is the most likely candidate based on visual inspection
Critical infrastructure identification from a street map tile is inherently uncertain — hospitals or emergency facilities may exist in this zone but not be visually distinguishable at this zoom level
